extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in scientometrics, science policy, and social science studying peer review, gender bias, and research evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: A quantitative research study replicating and extending Wennerås & Wold by analyzing new grant applications to the Swedish Medical Research Council, using normalization of ranks and bibliometrics and regression models with interactions to detect nepotism and gender effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalisation method for ranking applications across committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Introducing a normalisation method for ranking applications that takes into account the differences between committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing application scores or ranks from multiple review committees, apply a normalization procedure that adjusts for inter-committee differences so that rankings are comparable across committees. This reduces bias arising from committee-specific scoring tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalisation of bibliometric measures by field
rubrics_metrics.description: We also use a normalisation of bibliometric measures by field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust bibliometric indicators (e.g., publication or citation counts, impact scores) to field-specific baselines or distributions to account for disciplinary differences in publication and citation practices before using them as predictors or comparators in analyses of peer review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression analysis with interaction effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Finally, we perform a regression analysis with interaction effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multivariable regression models that include interaction terms (for example, gender × reviewer affiliation) to detect conditional effects and to distinguish main effects from joint-effects (e.g., whether reviewer affiliation modifies the gender effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an appropriate sample of applications (new applications to the funding body)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a replication of the high-profile contribution by Wennerås and Wold on grant peer-review, we investigate new applications processed by the medical research council in Sweden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base analyses on a clearly defined and relevant sample (here: new applications processed by the funding agency) to ensure findings reflect current/targeted review decisions rather than resubmissions or non-comparable application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and extension of prior influential studies
rubrics_metrics.description: A replication of the high-profile contribution by Wennerås and Wold on grant peer-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When replicating influential prior research, follow core elements of the original methodology while transparently documenting extensions or methodological improvements (such as normalization procedures) to assess persistence or change in the phenomenon (e.g., nepotism, gender bias).
